name: Clicker
subtitle: Drive game progression through high-frequency clicking.
concept: Click mechanics center around continuous player taps as the primary input. Each tap triggers immediate feedback—numeric jumps, sound cues, and synchronized animation. The core design balances feedback intensity against player fatigue, and aligns the reward curve with progression arcs. Overly strong visual/audio cues can cause short-term overstimulation, breaking flow; too weak cues lose instant gratification. The reward curve must provide sufficient early momentum while sustaining long-term viability to prevent churn. As click rewards gradually upgrade into automated output, the gameplay naturally transitions to idle, forming a growth arc from active operation to passive income—a foundational structure for long‑term retention in clicker games.
role: Provides an instant feedback loop, allowing players to confirm each click’s effectiveness immediately and maintain short‑term flow.
significance: It is the foundation of low‑barrier, high‑feedback gameplay and serves as the bridge for transitioning from active operation to passive income, shaping the growth arc from clicking to idle.
problemsSolved: Engage players with minimal operational cost
Maintain short‑term retention through continuous feedback
Transform clicking behavior into long‑term goals via upgrades
learningGoals: Design instant feedback and visual/audio amplification, balancing flow and fatigue
Build early incentive and long‑term sustainability in the click reward curve
Implement automation conversion mechanisms to reduce player fatigue
Balance the complementary relationship between clicking and idle to form a growth arc
Identify and avoid counterintuitive traps that cause loss of flow due to excessive mechanization
minimalRules: Players generate resources or effects through clicking
Click rewards can be upgraded to increase the value per click
There is a path to convert clicks into permanent growth
Set cooldowns or rate limits to prevent excessive clicking and fatigue

combos.effect: Active clicking complements passive income, creating continuous output
Clicking within specific windows grants bonuses, enhancing rhythm
Click rewards permanently upgrade, forming long‑term goals

advancedWarnings: Pure clicking can cause fatigue; provide automation or rhythm variation
Ensure the click reward curve does not start too slow or explode too late
Pay attention to mobile click hot zones and accidental taps
Avoid over‑reliance on a single click reward to prevent gameplay monotony

Design of critical hit / combo probabilities
